title: The vacant judgment-seat
summary: After Moronihah had established peace between the Nephites and Lamanites, the judgment-seat was vacant and contention arose over who should fill it.

explicit_facts.text: In the forty-second year of the judges, Moronihah had established peace between the Nephites and the Lamanites.
No one filled the judgment-seat, and contention arose over who should fill it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people can be shown disputing over the vacant judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and appearance of the judgment-seat and the identities or appearance of the disputants are unspecified.

narration.text: there began to be a contention again among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moronihah’s peace is prior context, not a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Moronihah establishing peace in this scene.
Do not invent the disputants’ words.

title: Helaman appointed
summary: The people appointed Helaman, son of Helaman, to fill the judgment-seat.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman, son of Helaman, was appointed to fill the judgment-seat by the voice of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman may be shown among the people at his appointment.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, appointment procedure, and appearance of the people are unspecified.

narration.text: appointed to fill the judgment-seat, by the voice of the people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent ceremony or exact words spoken by the people.

title: Gadianton leads the band
summary: Kishkumen and his band sought to destroy Helaman. Gadianton became the band’s leader and promised its members power and authority if they placed him in the judgment-seat.

explicit_facts.text: Kishkumen, who had murdered Pahoran, lay in wait to destroy Helaman, supported by his band, which covenanted to conceal its wickedness.
Gadianton, skilled in words and in secret murder and robbery, became leader of Kishkumen’s band.
Gadianton promised power and authority to band members if they placed him in the judgment-seat; Kishkumen therefore sought to destroy Helaman.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The band may be shown together with Gadianton and Kishkumen, without invented insignia or ritual.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place, clothing, and appearance of the band are unspecified.

narration.text: they should be placed in power and authority among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Pahoran’s murder is prior context, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Pahoran or his murder.
Do not add covenant wording or further plans.

title: The servant meets Kishkumen
summary: As Kishkumen went toward the judgment-seat to murder Helaman, he met Helaman’s servant, who had learned the band’s plan through disguise. The servant gave a sign, learned Kishkumen’s purpose, and invited him to go to the judgment-seat.

explicit_facts.text: Kishkumen went toward the judgment-seat to destroy Helaman; a servant of Helaman had learned the band’s plan through disguise.
The servant met Kishkumen and gave him a sign; Kishkumen asked to be conducted to the judgment-seat so he could murder Helaman.
The servant learned the band’s aims and said, “Let us go forth unto the judgment-seat.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: The meeting may be shown, without specifying the sign or the servant’s disguise.
unspecified_visual_details: The place of meeting, the sign, and the appearance of the disguise are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let us go forth unto the judgment-seat.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman’s servant

narration.text: he gave unto him a sign

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The servant’s night outing and intelligence-gathering are reported prior actions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the earlier night reconnaissance as a present event.
Do not show Helaman as present.
Do not add dialogue for Kishkumen.

title: Kishkumen is killed
summary: As Kishkumen and the servant went toward the judgment-seat, the servant stabbed Kishkumen, who fell dead without a groan.

explicit_facts.text: The servant stabbed Kishkumen to the heart, and Kishkumen fell dead without a groan.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The stabbing may be depicted without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place and weapon’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: did stab Kishkumen even to the heart

prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood, wounds, gore, or an unmentioned struggle.

title: The servant reports
summary: The servant ran and told Helaman all he had seen, heard, and done.

explicit_facts.text: The servant ran and told Helaman all the things he had seen, heard, and done.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The servant may be shown reporting to Helaman.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the content of the report are unspecified.

narration.text: he ran and told Helaman all the things which he had seen

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the report’s wording or details.

title: Helaman sends to take the band
summary: Helaman sent to take the band of robbers and secret murderers so they could be executed according to law.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman sent to take the band of robbers and secret murderers for execution according to law.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman may be shown sending others to take the band.
unspecified_visual_details: The messengers, location, and form of the order are unspecified.

narration.text: that they might be executed according to the law.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an execution; it is only the purpose of Helaman’s order.

title: Gadianton and the band flee
summary: When Kishkumen did not return, Gadianton feared destruction and caused his band to follow him. They fled by a secret way into the wilderness, and Helaman’s searchers could not find them.

explicit_facts.text: When Kishkumen did not return, Gadianton feared he would be destroyed and caused the band to follow him.
The band fled the land by a secret way into the wilderness; Helaman’s searchers could not find them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gadianton and the band may be shown fleeing into the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and appearance of the wilderness are unspecified.

narration.text: they took their flight out of the land, by a secret way, into the wilderness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The failed search is reported, not a separate encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict searchers confronting the band.
Do not invent the secret route.

title: The record’s closing note
summary: The account marks the end of the forty-second year, says more will be spoken about Gadianton, foretells his role in the near-destruction of the people of Nephi, and clarifies which book’s end it means.

explicit_facts.text: The forty-second year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi ended; more about Gadianton would be spoken later.
The account says Gadianton would prove the overthrow, almost the entire destruction, of the people of Nephi.
The speaker means the end of the book of Nephi, not the end of the book of Helaman.

unspecified_visual_details: No visible setting or narrator is specified.

narration.text: And more of this Gadianton shall be spoken hereafter.
And thus ended the forty and second year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.
this Gadianton did prove the overthrow
I do not mean the end of the book of Helaman, but I mean the end of the book of Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The foretold overthrow is not a present event in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the foretold destruction as a present event.
Do not add a visible narrator or record-keeper.
